entry.title: [BIP Draft] Co-signer Spending Policies
entry.summary:
Once the protocol achieves interoperability across lenders, borrowers gain the ability to transfer or refinance loans with different financial institutions seamlessly. This eliminates the need to liquidate Bitcoin holdings or relinquish custody, preserving both ownership and flexibility throughout the loan process.
Increased portability of assets fosters robust competition among lenders, driving better rates and services for borrowers. No single lender retains exclusive control over customer assets, ensuring a more equitable environment and preventing monopolistic practices. The protocol’s compatibility enables any wallet to interact with any lending institution, oracle, or co-signer, mitigating the risk of centralized points of failure and enhancing system resilience.
Transparency is significantly enhanced through auditability, allowing anyone to review and verify loan policies prior to funding. This replaces reliance on institutional assurances with clear, verifiable rules, thereby reducing the necessity for blind trust and empowering users to make informed decisions.
The adoption of standardized infrastructure lowers entry barriers for new lenders, who can integrate into the existing ecosystem without the burden of developing comprehensive systems from scratch. Moreover, the protocol’s versatility extends its utility beyond traditional lending, supporting use cases such as digital vaults, escrow arrangements, inheritance planning, and spending controls for AI agents.
It is important to acknowledge that while this framework streamlines and standardizes the level of trust required in co-signers, it does not render them entirely trustless nor does it resolve outstanding legal complexities. Legal guidance remains essential to navigate these areas, but the protocol serves to minimize and clarify the scope of necessary trust within the system.
